findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
The bathroom that is off to the side of the bar is observed to have coving that is pulled away from the wall. There were observed to be multiple fast-moving roaches that came out of this coving when the coving was disturbed. 

In the main men’s bathroom, there were observed to be two dead baby roaches, one on the floor and one in the cabinets. 

In the kitchen, there was observed to be a fast-moving roach under the soda fountain area and another fast-moving roach in the back corner that went into coving that is pulled away from the wall. There were over a dozen dead roaches of all life stages on the floor throughout the kitchen. 

Throughout the kitchen, there is observed to be missing coving and coving that is no longer sealed to the wall. There is also observed to be cardboard that is being kept in the kitchen. There needs to be attention to cleaning as well to ensure that the dead roaches are being regularly cleaned up. The back door was observed to be cracked open, potentially allowing more pests to enter the facility. 

The PIC was unsure of where pest control records would be kept. In the past, Terminix and Bacon’s were listed as the pest control companies. The PIC stated that pest control has come frequently in the past two months. 

A follow up is scheduled for 8/3/2026 to ensure that cleaning is occurring throughout the facility to clean dead roaches, that pest control is regularly coming, and that proper actions are being taken by the facility to reduce pest presence (removing cardboard, keeping the back door shut, sealing coving, etc.).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector noted several live cockroaches on glue traps around the facility. All glue traps were observed to have some amount of cockroaches on them. PIC informed inspector that pest control comes once a week on Mondays. This indicates that pest control alone is not enough to keep the cockroach population down. Inspector recommends a deep cleaning of all dark and unused areas, as well as behind and inside equipment. Cockroaches can hide in these places and maintain a pest presence in the kitchen even when pest control is active. Ensure the cockroaches are eradicated to maintain clean and sanitary food-contact surfaces.

findings.comment:
Inspector observed the CFPM to not have an allergen certification. Talked with the CFPM about allergen certifications and provided the class handout. Ensure that all CFPMs on staff receive allergen training.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: Observed nearly sixteen Ziploc quart containers holding Spanish rice to be covered and stacked in the top of the glass sliding door cooler temped at 45-78F. It was stated the rice was cooked within the last hour or so, the rice was moved onto shallow pans, placed on the roll cart, and brought into the walk-in cooler. Foods need to be controlled during the cooling process. There is a stem thermometer and cooling log available (last dated entries were from 2021). Nicholas discussed cooling process with the cook and also discussed using the log. The facility is a Class I due to the cooling and reheating of foods. A significant number of foods are being cooled and reheated. See that cook staff is trained on cooling techniques and facility staff is all helping with this process.  
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 Cheese sauce was observed with an internal temperature of 107F in the steam table. Cheese sauce was placed directly in the steam table for reheating. Cheese sauce was placed on the grill to rapidly reheat to 165F prior to hot holding. Owner was advised to speak with staff regarding proper use of equipment for intended purposes. The steam table is intended to hold hot food at 135F/above after it has already been properly heated to required cook/reheat temperature. 
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds. This process should be done rapidly, within 2hrs or less, using equipment that is intended for cooking/reheating foods.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Three pans of refried beans with preparation dates of 10/21/21 in the walk-in cooler had internal temperatures of 50F; 48F; and 47F. Refried beans were discarded during inspection. Owner reiterated proper cooling in shallow pans with cook during inspection. Cook noted ice bath was used, but only the surface temperature was monitored using an infrared thermometer. Ensure internal temperatures are monitored during cooling process to verify foods are cooling quickly and properly. 
Cooked TCS foods shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and from 70F to 41F/below within an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hours. Utilize ice baths to chill smaller portions of foods quickly. Use a clean, calibrated food thermometer to monitor cooling TCS foods during the cooling process and ensure foods are reaching temperatures as required for the bench marks of proper cooling.

A designated PIC with a current food manger certification was not present upon arrival of inspector. Handwashing and cooling practices were discussed at length and will be revisited at spot check later this month. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Certified food manager was not present when inspector arrived at the facility for inspection. Owner has a current CFM and arrived at the facility later during the inspection. Owner was advised a designated PIC with a current food manager certification must be present during all hours of operation. Ensure that additional staff complete a food manager certification course by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM is on-site during all hours of operation, including when the owner leaves during periods of time in the afternoons.  
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed putting on gloves to prepare food without first washing their hands. Proper handwashing prior to glove use was discussed. Employee discarded gloves and washed hands prior to putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with food preparation. 
--Owner arrived to the facility and did not was hands prior to opening the oven and touching Spanish rice that was in the process of reheating. Handwashing upon entering the kitchen and prior to handling food was discussed. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and upon entering the work area.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 During handwashing, an employee was observed using paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet and then finished drying hands with the paper towels that were just used to shut off the faucet. Employee as advised hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. If additional drying of hands is needed, use fresh paper towels to finish drying hands. 
--Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Employees were observed making an effort to use proper handwashing technique for the remainder of inspection. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Pans with cooked beef and chicken were uncovered on one of the shelves in the walkin cooler. The shelving above had some debris accumulation and chipping paint. Covers were provided for the pans of food. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solution in kitchen sani-bucket was observed at concentration below 50ppm chlorine. Solution was discarded and fresh solution provided at 200ppm.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Ensure concentrations are no lower than no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm as directed by label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener was observed with debris on the blade. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during the inspection.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Cooked pork prepared earlier today was observed in a tub on a cooling rack in the kitchen. Surface and internal temperatures were observed at 94F and 102F-119F respectively. Kitchen staff indicated the pork started cooling 2hrs prior to when temperature was checked. Pork was reheated to 180F prior to restarting the cooling process. Ice baths were setup to help chill pork during cooling.  
--Spanish rice cooked earlier today was observed in several plastic containers stacked in the sliding door cooler. Internal temperatures were observed between 72F and 89F, with some portions observed at 80F and 85F. Spanish rice was past the first two hours of cooling time frame based on information provided. Cook time and temperature was not indicated on the cooling log. Rice was placed in the oven to reheat product to 165F prior to hot holding a portion and beginning cooling process again for the remainder.
-A portion of steak in the sliding door cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 86F. Steak was prepared earlier in the day. Cook indicated the steak in question was not needed and discarded it in the trash during the inspection. 
Cooked TCS foods shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and from 70F to 41F/below within an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hours. Utilize ice baths to chill smaller portions of foods quickly. Use a clean, calibrated food thermometer to monitor cooling TCS foods during the cooling process and ensure foods are reaching temperatures as required for the bench marks of proper cooling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Pan of cooked chicken in the walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 51F. Cook stated the chicken was heated at lunch time and then some of it was placed back in the walkin cooler. The portion at 51F was discarded during the inspection.
-Quinoa in the top holding area of one of the prep coolers had an internal temperature between 52F-54F. Quinoa was to be used or discarded by the end of operations this evening.
-A portion of white rice in the sliding door cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 51F. Warm Spanish rice in the process of cooling was placed on top of the container of white rice. Owner was advised to monitor temperatures of all foods in the sliding door cooler and use or discard the white rice by the end of operations this evening. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Cheese sauce and black beans were observed sitting out on a prep table upon arrival of inspector. Foods were still observed on the prep table an hour later. Surface temperatures were at 91F-96, while internal temperatures ranged from 131F to 153F. Ice baths were setup to start quick chill process. 
-Chile salsa bajillo (full 8qt container) and salsa picante (full 6qt container) prepared earlier in the day were in the walkin cooler and observed with internal temperatures at 112F and 89F respectively. Ice baths were setup to help cool sauces quicker.
Cooling smaller portions in ice baths and monitoring the temperature of cooling foods were discussed. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged fish were observed in the bottom holding area of a prep cooler. Proper thawing of fish in reduced oxygen packaging was discussed. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Floor fans were observed with buildup of dust and debris. Ensure floor fans are cleaned as needed to eliminate buildup.
--Shelving in walkin cooler was soiled with general buildup and paint was starting to chip away in a few areas. Clean the walkin cooler shelving and reseal any areas that appear rough from chipping paint. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: On arrival, no CFPM is observed at the facility. All Class I & Class II facilities are required to have a CFPM on site during operation. CFPM arrived during the inspection to correct.
